summary: Make the equipment split enforce unique instance ids, closing the second door to the entry-key collision class

Both bullets closed. Tree left dirty, nothing committed, `launch.json` untouched, my private server on 8791 stopped (the 8777 server belongs to another agent and was left alone).

## The repro, before and after

Driven through the real `migrate` (via `importCharacter` and `EN.store.load()`) and then on screen, with `equipment: [{id:"eq_DUP", name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty:1}, {same}]`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `ownedRigs` keys | `["eq_DUP","eq_DUP"]`, 1 distinct | `["eq_DUP","eq_ph72smj"]`, 2 distinct |
| 23 damage on the picked rig | `hp: {eq_DUP: 23}`, **both** rows read `17/40` | only `eq_DUP` reads `17/40`; the other reads `40/40` |
| picker options | `key:eq_DUP` / `key:eq_DUP`, browser selects the last, `#1` unaddressable | `key:eq_DUP` / `key:eq_ph72smj`, both selectable |
| Fabrication bench | medkit chip printed **twice** | printed **once**, Medtech `Edge 3` |

After the fix I drove real damage through the actual DAMAGE button: 23 on `#1`, 31 on `#2`, holding independently at `17/40` and `9/40`, surviving a switch between them and a full page reload.

## What I changed

`app/js/store.js` only, both inside the equipment split.

1. **Id uniqueness, `:328-402`.** A pre-pass collects every id the incoming list carries into `reservedIds`; `usedIds` tracks what has actually been handed out, in list order. A row whose id is already in `usedIds` gets a fresh one from `mintId()`, which draws until it hits an id in neither set. The split's own minting (`:392`) now goes through the same `mintId()`.
2. **`ch.racked` added to the rekey pass, `:421-434`**, rekeying keys and values, since it maps an entry to an entry. Genuinely mechanical, so I did it.

## Proof the fix is a no-op for unique-id records

Not asserted. 34 migration shapes, each loaded, written back, and re-loaded twice more, with `Math.random` stubbed by a seeded LCG so minted ids are reproducible and a pre-fix run is comparable byte for byte. Every shape's **entire migrated record** was fingerprinted, not just the fields I touched.

- **26 of 26 shapes without a duplicate id hash identically to the pre-fix run** — including the 11 that mint ids, which is the load-bearing part: `mintId()` draws exactly one random number per instance in the no-collision case, so the RNG sequence is unchanged.
- Exactly 7 shapes changed: the 6 carrying duplicate ids, plus the racked one.
- Zero throws; **zero unstable across three loads** (pre-fix, the racked shape was the one that was not stable).
- All six tiers re-verified: Output `+0/+1/+1/+2/+2/+3`, Triage Save DC `8/9/9/10/10/11` at Tech +0, Mod Slots = Tier, traits 1-6, Integrity `15/20/25/30/35/40`, nodes Standard through Apex, medkit flipping to Advanced at Trauma Grade [2]. All seven tabs render with zero console errors for a Stitcher and for a non-Stitcher holding two rigs.

## Per-entry state on the re-idded row

First seen keeps the original id, so `ch.rig.key`, `ch.rig.hp`, `carry`, `slotInert`, `racked` and the equip slots keep pointing at the row they always meant. The re-idded row starts with **no** per-entry state and arrives at full Integrity — the settled ruling that unattributable state is dropped rather than duplicated. Verified: in the duplicate-weapon shape, `equippedWeapons`, `carry` and `slotInert` all still resolve to row 1, and row 2 is a clean spare.

## Can a minted id collide?

Handled, and forced rather than argued. With the seeded RNG the first mint is always `eq_3vvy44y`, so I planted that exact id on a pre-existing row in both orders. Mint-first-then-pre-existing: `reservedIds` had already claimed it, so the split minted `eq_lvx1gzh` and the pre-existing row kept its id, its recorded pick and its 9 damage. Pre-existing-first-then-mint: same outcome. **Without the pre-pass the first case would have let a minted id steal an id a later row legitimately owned** — that is why the reservation scans the whole list up front instead of only tracking what it has seen so far.

I also widened "carries an id" from a string check to the same truthy test the skip clause uses, so two rows sharing `id: 5` and `id: "5"` collide as one key and are separated (they coerce to one object key, exactly as `entryKey` would resolve them).

## `ch.racked`

Done, and the existing write-up understated it. The omission did not merely orphan a rack: load 1 rekeyed `carry` to ids and left `racked` on its dead name key, then load 2's carry sanitizer (`app/js/store.js:199`, which downgrades a `"racked"` status whose target is missing) rewrote it to `"carried"`. It was **the only shape in the whole set that failed the three-load stability check**, before or after. After the fix it migrates to `racked: {eq_x: eq_y}`, is stable across three loads, and renders live: Loadout reads "1 racked", the Dagger nests under the Sheath with `⧉ RACKS 1/1` and `⧉ Racked: Sheath`, and its Load drops by 1.

## `DEFERRED-FIXES.md`

Closed both bullets with before-and-after numbers and added a verification-run section. Also corrected what went stale: the racked gap is no longer listed as open in the three other places that named it (the blast-radius section, GROUP C, GROUP D); GROUP C now states the stronger invariant; the Armor Repair recommendation gained a "second and a half" done item; reason 2 of the Armor Repair argument was re-scoped since the identity it worried about now exists; and the line references the split's growth moved (L8, L9, L10, L11, L13, the `firstKeyOfTier` pointer) were updated, with a one-line note that older numbers in that section predate the change.

Untouched as instructed: `shieldWear`, armor state, Open Architecture, every tier value and derived rig field. The `nameToIds` last-write-wins nit stays open and is unrelated (two rows sharing a NAME, not an id).

Environment: my own origin `http://localhost:8794`, forced reload before every reading (`EN.traumaRigs` confirmed present), roster snapshotted and restored, my server stopped, my `launch.json` entry removed. Tree left dirty, no git state changed. Another agent's `app/__refute2/` was left alone.

## FINDING 1 (CONFIRMED, introduced by this change) — prototype-key ids defeat the uniqueness check, and the row that owns the id is the one that loses it

`app/js/store.js:354`

```js
var reservedIds = {}, usedIds = {};
```

Both are plain object literals, so the collision test at `:369` (`if (usedIds[e.id]) e.id = mintId();`) reads through `Object.prototype`. **A row whose `id` is an `Object.prototype` property name is judged a duplicate even when it is the only row in the list carrying it**, and is silently re-idded.

Failing scenario, measured through the real `migrate` via `EN.store.load()`:

| input | migrated row id | `rig.key` | `rig.hp` | `rigStats` reports |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[{id:"eq_norm", name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty:1}]`, `rig:{key:"eq_norm", hp:{eq_norm:23}}` | `eq_norm` (kept) | `eq_norm` | `{eq_norm:23}` | **17 / 40** |
| same record, id `"constructor"` | **`eq_ekap5ly`** | `"constructor"` | `{constructor:23}` | **40 / 40, spent 0** |

The second record has **one** rig and **no** duplicate id. It is not the shape the fix targets, and pre-fix it migrated untouched (the diff adds the only code that mutates `e.id`). The 23 points of recorded damage and the recorded pick are both gone from the sheet.

It compounds with an existing prototype hole in the block below: `liveKeys` at `:466-467` is also a `{}`, so `liveKeys["constructor"]` is truthy, and the prune at `:477-481` and the pick-clear at `:482` both spare the now-dead keys. The record is left with `rig.key:"constructor"` and `rig.hp:{constructor:23}` pointing at nothing, permanently.

It also breaks the "first seen keeps the original id" rule outright — the *first* row is the one that gets moved:

```
[{id:"toString", name:R, qty:1}, {id:"eq_other", name:R, qty:1}]
  ->  ["eq_bmgvq5u", "eq_other"]      // first seen did NOT keep its id
```

Reproduced for `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `isPrototypeOf`, `toLocaleString`, `propertyIsEnumerable`, and `__proto__` (the last for the extra reason that `usedIds["__proto__"] = 1` is a discarded assignment, so the reservation never lands either).

Fix is one line: `var reservedIds = Object.create(null), usedIds = Object.create(null);`. Worth doing the same to `nameToIds` at `:327` and `liveKeys` at `:466` while there — `nameToIds` has the identical hole today and turns a `carry` key of `"constructor"` into the literal string `"null"` (`firstId()` at `:404` returns `null` because `Object.prototype.constructor[0]` is `undefined`); that part is pre-existing and unchanged by this work.

Reachability is hand-authored records and imports only, which is exactly the threat model the fix argues from ("Reachable by import and by hand-authored records"), but a much narrower slice of it than a copy-pasted duplicate. Severity is low; the objection is that the report's headline safety claim, "it must be a no-op for records whose ids are already unique, prove that, do not assert it", is **false as stated**, and the 34-shape fingerprint run did not cover this shape.

## FINDING 2 (residual) — `DEFERRED-FIXES.md:853-854` states an invariant the fix does not deliver

> "Entry identity is now complete: **every equipment row's `entryKey` is unique after migration**, whether it arrived with an id, without one, or with somebody else's."

Uniqueness is enforced over **ids**, never over the effective `entryKey` (`e.id || e.name`, `app/js/engine.js:871`). Four measured counterexamples, all after migration:

| record | resulting keys |
|---|---|
| `[{name:"Pistol Ammo",qty:2},{name:"Pistol Ammo",qty:3}]` | `["Pistol Ammo","Pistol Ammo"]` |
| `[{name:"Homebrew Widget",qty:1},{name:"Homebrew Widget",qty:1}]` | `["Homebrew Widget","Homebrew Widget"]` |
| `[{name:R,qty:0},{name:R,qty:0}]` (unowned rigs) | `[R, R]` |
| `[{name:"Pistol Ammo",qty:2},{id:"Pistol Ammo",name:R,qty:1}]` | `["Pistol Ammo","Pistol Ammo"]`, and `ownedRigs` returns `["Pistol Ammo"]` |

The first three are benign (pooled stacks, and unowned rows the engine excludes) and pre-existing. The fourth is a genuine cross-type collision the fix does not catch, though it needs a hand-authored id equal to another row's catalog name. None is a regression. The claim itself is also self-contradicted twelve lines later by the surviving `nameToIds` last-write-wins bullet at `:891`, which concedes two rows can share a name. Soften the sentence to what was actually proved: *every row that carries an id ends up with an id no other row carries.* Relatedly, `:500-501` says the name branch "now serves only pooled stackables"; it also serves unowned non-stackable rows.

## FINDING — `app/js/store.js:355` and `:368-371`: the uniqueness pass uses bare `{}` maps, so an id that names an `Object.prototype` member is treated as a duplicate on first sight and silently re-idded, destroying that row's per-entry state

`var reservedIds = {}, usedIds = {};` then `if (usedIds[e.id]) e.id = mintId();`. `usedIds` is a plain object, so `usedIds["toString"]`, `["constructor"]`, `["hasOwnProperty"]`, `["valueOf"]`, `["__proto__"]`, `["isPrototypeOf"]`, `["propertyIsEnumerable"]`, `["toLocaleString"]` all return an inherited truthy value. The very first row carrying such an id collides with nothing yet is re-idded anyway.

Failing scenario, driven through the real `migrate` on a booted page (localhost:8817, forced reload), with **one** rig row and **one** unique id:

```
equipment: [{ id: "toString", name: "Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty: 1 }]
rig: { key: "toString", scrap: false, hp: { toString: 23 } }
```

| `EN.engine.derive(ch).rig` | pre-fix (HEAD) | post-fix (working tree) |
|---|---|---|
| `rigKey` | `toString` | `eq_16eip91` |
| `integritySpent` | **23** | **0** |
| `integrity` (remaining) | **17** | **40** |
| `fromOwnedGear` | false (pick honored) | true (pick lost, fell back to AUTO) |

The row's id is rewritten, so `rig.key` and `rig.hp` are orphaned: `ch.equipment.some(e => EN.engine.entryKey(e) === ch.rig.key)` is `false` after. 23 points of Integrity damage and the recorded pick are erased. This is the exact loss the whole change exists to prevent, now inflicted on a record whose ids were already unique.

It is also unrecoverable rather than transient. The rig prune at `store.js:477` (`if (!liveKeys[k] ...) delete rg.hp[k]`) and the pick clear at `:482` (`if (rg.key && !liveKeys[rg.key])`) read the same bare-object `liveKeys`, so `liveKeys["toString"]` is truthy and the dead key is never reaped. The orphaned `hp` entry and `key` survive every subsequent load. Verified: post-fix output is byte-stable across three loads with the garbage still in place.

`equippedWeapons`, `carry`, `slotInert` and `racked` on such a row are separately mangled, but that part is pre-existing (`nameToIds[name]` at `:406`/`:413`/`:418` has the same prototype exposure and produced the identical `carry: {"null": "worn"}` in both variants), so it is not attributable to this change. The rig loss is.

Reachability is the same threat model the fix's own comment claims for the defect it closes: import and hand-authored records. No in-app path mints a proto-key id, so severity is low. The one-line fixes are `Object.create(null)` for `reservedIds`/`usedIds` (and `liveKeys`), or `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(usedIds, e.id)`.

### 1. The invariant the write-up now sells to step 5 is true per ROW and false per PIECE (`app/js/store.js:388`)

The skip clause is still `if (e.id || !(e.qty > 0) || stackable)`. The fix closed "two rows, one id"; it did not touch "**one row, one id, `qty: N`**", because `e.id` short-circuits before the split ever looks at `qty`. That is the same short-circuit the fix was written to close, reached through the other operand.

Failing scenario, measured on screen: `equipment: [{id:"eq_x", name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty:3}]`, `rig:{key:"eq_x", hp:{eq_x:23}}`. This matters because `DEFERRED-FIXES.md` now states, twice, that the floor step 5 stands on is **"after migration, no two equipment rows share an `entryKey`"**, and adds "so two Kevlar Weaves cannot share a repair state no matter how the record was authored." Authored as `{id:"eq_a", name:"Kevlar Weave", qty:2}` they will share one repair state, because they are one row. The claim as written is literally true and operationally insufficient; the statement step 5 actually needs is per-piece, not per-row.

Reachability is import / hand-authored only, the same class as the duplicate-id defect that was just fixed on that basis (`inventory.js:106` and `builder.js:993` both mint one id per non-stackable purchase at `qty: 1`, confirmed). Pre-existing, not introduced. Either split an id-carrying non-stackable row with `qty > 1` the same way, or narrow the doc's claim so step 5 does not inherit a floor it cannot stand on.

### 2. `reservedIds` / `usedIds` are bare object literals, so eight unique ids are misread as duplicates (`app/js/store.js:354`, detected at `:369`)

`var reservedIds = {}, usedIds = {};` inherits `Object.prototype`, so `usedIds[e.id]` is truthy on **first sight** for `id` values `constructor`, `valueOf`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `isPrototypeOf`, `propertyIsEnumerable`, `toLocaleString` and `__proto__`. A row whose id is unique is re-idded, and per the fix's own rule the re-idded row starts with no per-entry state. That is a counterexample to "it must be a no-op for records whose ids are already unique", which the report calls the whole safety argument.

Failing scenario, run against both stores in the same page:

    equipment: [{id:"constructor", name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty:1}]
    rig: {key:"constructor", hp:{constructor:23}}

| | pre-fix (`HEAD`) | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| row id | `constructor` | `eq_oohnuqo` |
| resolved `rigKey` | `constructor` | `eq_oohnuqo` |
| Integrity | `17/40` | `40/40` (23 points gone) |
| `rig.hp` | `{constructor: 23}` | `{constructor: 23}`, now an orphan |

The orphan is not even pruned, because `liveKeys` at `app/js/store.js:466` has the same shape and `liveKeys["constructor"]` is truthy, so `rig.key` also stays `"constructor"` forever. That half and the `carry`/`slotInert` keys collapsing to the literal string `"null"` are **pre-existing** (`nameToIds` at `:327` has the same hole and produced them identically on the pre-fix run) — the re-idding, and the damage loss it causes, are new. `Object.create(null)` for `reservedIds`, `usedIds`, and while nearby `nameToIds` and `liveKeys`, closes all of it. Severity low: hand-edit/import only, eight magic strings.

### Nit, documentation only

The new "Verification run" section does not add up: 34 shapes, "all twenty-six shapes without a duplicate id hash identically", "exactly seven shapes changed". 26 + 7 = 33. One shape is unaccounted for in the prose.
